diagnosis: Newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS; ICD-10-CM C83.30, SNOMED CT 109969005), non-germinal-center B-cell (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm. Diagnosis is established on excisional biopsy of the left cervical level IV node collected 2026-09-09 (final report 2026-09-11, amended 2026-09-16 with the FISH addendum): diffuse sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells, centroblastic with focal immunoblastic morphology, numerous mitoses and focal necrosis, effaced architecture; CD20+ (diffuse strong), PAX5+, CD3-/CD5-/CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1/IRF4 ~70%, BCL2 ~80%, MYC ~50%, cyclin D1-, CD30-, Ki-67 ~85%, EBER-ISH negative, lambda-restricted by flow. FISH on 200 nuclei is negative for MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21) and BCL6 (3q27) rearrangements. This excludes double-hit and triple-hit lymphoma (high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements), so the disease is managed as conventional DLBCL-NOS and DA-R-EPOCH-R is not required; EBER negativity excludes EBV-associated DLBCL, and CD30 negativity excludes PMBCL (which would also be inconsistent with the multifocal disease distribution). There is no history or morphologic evidence of an underlying indolent lymphoma (i.e., no transformation). Presenting features are characteristic: 3 months of progressive painless left cervical adenopathy, B symptoms (evening fever to 38.5 C several nights weekly, drenching night sweats, ~7 kg unintentional weight loss), a large FDG-avid retroperitoneal nodal mass, and FDG-avid splenic lesions.
stage: Lugano stage III with splenic involvement (IIIS), PET-CT staged (2026-09-05), equivalent to Ann Arbor III2-S; bulky; B symptoms present. Disease involves nodal regions on both sides of the diaphragm - left cervical levels III-IV (largest 3.1 x 2.4 cm, SUVmax 18.7), right paratracheal (2.6 cm, SUVmax 15.2) and subcarinal (2.2 cm, SUVmax 13.9) nodes above, and a confluent left para-aortic/aortocaval retroperitoneal mass 11.0 x 8.1 cm (SUVmax 22.4) below - plus splenic involvement (spleen 14.2 cm with at least four FDG-avid hypodense lesions, largest 2.4 cm, SUVmax 16.3). The 11 cm retroperitoneal mass meets the >=10 cm definition of bulky disease. Two points of staging logic are worth stating at the board: (1) the spleen is a lymphatic organ, so splenic involvement is annotated 'S' and does not make this stage IV; (2) stage IV here would require parenchymal extranodal disease or marrow involvement, and the right posterior iliac crest aspirate/biopsy (2026-09-12, normocellular, trilineage hematopoiesis, no morphologic disease, negative CD20/PAX5 stains, no monotypic B-cell population on flow) is negative. There is no FDG-avid disease in liver, lung, bone, marrow, kidneys, adrenals, bowel, testes or CNS, and no pleural/pericardial effusion. Splenic involvement is radiologic rather than biopsy-proven, but this does not alter management.
biology: CD20-positive/PAX5-positive mature B-cell neoplasm, non-GCB (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive in ~70% of cells, Hans algorithm). Two adverse biologic features: (1) IHC double expressor - MYC protein in ~50% of tumor cells (>=40%) and BCL2 protein in ~80% (>=50%); and (2) high proliferative index (Ki-67 ~85%) with immunoblastic features and focal necrosis. Critically, FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements, so this is NOT double-hit/triple-hit disease; double-expressor status is a prognostic label only and does not change the recommended first-line regimen or move the patient to DA-R-EPOCH-R. Non-GCB subtype and double-expressor status are both independent adverse prognostic features (worse PFS/OS than GCB and non-double-expressor patients) and are the principal reasons I favor the pola-R-CHP backbone rather than plain R-CHOP, since the benefit of polatuzumab in the POLO trial was seen across subgroups including non-GCB and double-expressor patients. EBER negative (no EBV-associated disease and no need for EBV-directed therapy or consideration of rituximab if it were positive); CD30 negative (brentuximab not indicated); cyclin D1 negative (excludes mantle cell involvement); no EBV/monoclonal gammopathy workup required; lambda-restricted by flow confirms clonality. Per NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (DLBCL), a double expressor without rearrangement does not warrant escalation of chemotherapy or a trial-type addition of a targeted agent outside a clinical trial.
prognosis: International Prognostic Index 2 (low-intermediate risk) and NCCN-IPI approximately 3 (high-intermediate risk), with the LDH ratio uncertain because the laboratory upper limit of normal is not provided. IPI components: age >60 (62 years) = 1; LDH elevated (680 U/L on 09-03, 735 U/L on 09-16) = 1; ECOG <2 (1) = 0; stage III/IV = 1; extranodal sites >1 = 0 (spleen is a lymphatic organ, not an extranodal site) - total 2. NCCN-IPI adds albumin 3.7 g/dL (>=3.5, so 0 points) and the LDH ratio (>1.0 certainly, possibly >1.5 depending on ULN), giving 3-4. With R-CHOP-class therapy I expect roughly 60-70% 5-year overall survival and ~50-60% 5-year PFS for IPI 2, and the POLO trial (SITC/Alliance) showed that adding polatuzumab to R-CHP in IPI 2-5 improved 2-year OS (86.7% vs 75.1%) and PFS (median 27.5 vs 21.7 months; HR for death 0.59, HR for PFS 0.72), which is the basis for my choice below. Adverse features not captured by IPI that lower my expectation: non-GCB subtype, IHC double expressor (MYC 50%/BCL2 80%), bulky 11 cm disease, B symptoms, and an LDH that is rising (680 to 735 U/L in 13 days) - this is a clinically active, bulky, symptomatic disease that should be treated promptly rather than staged further. Primary risks to the plan are (a) primary refractory disease (~20-25% of patients do not achieve CR on first-line therapy), for which I have pre-specified a biopsy and switch strategy rather than continuing the same regimen, and (b) CNS relapse risk, which is addressed under CNS risk.
first_line_treatment: Six cycles of polatuzumab vedotin + R-CHP (pola-R-CHP) every 21 days, started as soon as possible after the tumor board (target cycle 1 the week of 2026-09-28; every day counts here given bulky disease, B symptoms and rising LDH). Dosing per cycle: polatuzumab vedotin 1.45 mg/kg IV (weight-based, ~115 mg for 79 kg) on day 1 over ~90 minutes, rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, and prednisone 100 mg on days 1-5; cycles 1-6, with a 21-day cycle length and a 1-week interval between cycles. Reasons for this specific choice: (1) he is advanced stage (III) with IPI 2, which is exactly the POLO population in which NCCN lists pola-R-CHP as a preferred regimen for previously untreated DLBCL with IPI 2-5; (2) it preserves a curative intent while adding benefit in the adverse biology he has (non-GCB, double expressor); (3) his baseline echocardiogram is normal (LVEF 58%, GLS -20%), so full-dose doxorubicin is appropriate; (4) he has no contraindications to polatuzumab (no peripheral neuropathy on exam, normal LFTs, no diabetes/ocular disease). Polatuzumab is discontinued at cycle 6. If polatuzumab is not covered/available, plain R-CHOP x6 cycles is a fully acceptable alternative and I would not delay treatment on the basis of a coverage dispute; I would not substitute DA-R-EPOCH-R (no MYC/BCL2 rearrangement) and would not add maintenance therapy or a non-standard targeted agent. I will also screen at the tumor board for an open first-line trial in advanced-stage DLBCL (ideally one enrolling non-GCB/double-expressor patients); if an appropriate trial is available and he is eligible and willing, I will offer it as an alternative to pola-R-CHP, and otherwise proceed with the regimen above. Concurrent with chemo: intrathecal CNS prophylaxis (see CNS risk), pegfilgrastim with every cycle, PET-adapted interim assessment after cycle 2 (see response assessment), and echocardiogram with GLS after every 2 cycles (before cycle 3 and cycle 5, and at completion) with a plan to drop doxorubicin or substitute if LVEF falls below 50% or GLS falls below 15% from baseline. Because he is only mildly anemic (Hb 10.8, MCV 88, normal WBC/ANC/platelets) with no cytopenias, no dose reductions are planned and I will dose on actual body weight (79 kg, BSA 1.98 m2).
cns_risk: Intermediate CNS relapse risk; CNS prophylaxis is indicated and a brain MRI is required before treatment. CNS-IPI = 3 points: age >60 (1), LDH above ULN (1), stage III (1); no points for ECOG >=2, >1 extranodal site, or kidney/adrenal involvement, and no 4-point penalty for MYC/BCL2-rearranged high-grade B-cell lymphoma because FISH is negative. Although the historical NCCN trigger list (adrenal, kidney, breast, testicular or vertebral/paravertebral involvement; MYC/BCL2 rearrangement; elevated LDH with high IPI) is not formally met, he has three recognized risk factors (LDH elevation, stage III-IV, age >60) and a CNS-IPI in the intermediate-risk band, and the recent IL-1 and BTK inhibitor experience has made the consequences of CNS relapse in DLBCL markedly worse. My decision: (1) obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI before cycle 1 - the PET report explicitly states that PET is insensitive for intracranial disease, and no brain imaging exists; (2) give intrathecal cytarabine plus methotrexate (with dexamethasone) with each of the 6 systemic cycles, or per institutional protocol on cycle days 1 and 4 (evidence for intrathecal prophylaxis is weak and practice varies, which is why I state the rationale explicitly); (3) no systemic high-dose methotrexate or high-dose cytarabine is required, as there is no documented CNS involvement; (4) document a neurologic examination at every visit and re-evaluate immediately for headache, cranial nerve symptoms, confusion, weakness or seizures - if any occur I will obtain MRI with gadolinium +/- CSF cytology/flow and involve neurology. Note there is no testicular involvement on PET or exam, so testicular ultrasound is not indicated, and I will not add CNS-directed treatment to the bulky retroperitoneal disease (no vertebral, renal or adrenal involvement).
response_assessment: PET-adapted approach using the same scanner/protocol as the 2026-09-05 baseline study (baseline reference SUVmax: retroperitoneal mass 22.4, cervical node 18.7, splenic lesion 16.3). Interim PET-CT after cycle 2 (before cycle 3), which NCCN specifically recommends for bulky disease: Deauville 1-3 (or Lugano interim change from baseline of >50% reduction to a Deauville 4-5 lesion) is a negative interim scan and I will complete the planned 6 cycles; Deauville 4-5 with residual FDG uptake is a positive interim scan, and I will image with contrast CT/MRI as needed and biopsy the most FDG-avid site before altering therapy - because ~50% of interim PET-positive lesions are false positives (inflammation, treatment effect, rituximab-related uptake) and I will not abandon a curative regimen on imaging alone. If the interim biopsy shows persistent DLBCL, I will switch to salvage therapy (R-DHAP or R-ICE x3-4) with high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation for chemosensitive disease, and will refer early for CAR-T (axi-cel or liso-cel) evaluation; if he is not a transplant candidate I will use the bispecific antibody (with or without lenalidomide) or CAR-T pathway per NCCN. End-of-treatment PET-CT 4-6 weeks after cycle 6 (~February-March 2027): Deauville 1-3 is complete metabolic response (Lugano CR) and, with no other concerns, he moves to surveillance with no additional therapy; Deauville 4-5 (partial metabolic response) requires biopsy of the residual FDG-avid site to distinguish residual lymphoma from scar/inflammation, and a positive biopsy triggers salvage chemoimmunotherapy and transplant or CAR-T as above; new or progressive FDG-avid lesions define progression and are treated as refractory/relapsed disease. Surveillance: I will obtain a follow-up PET-CT 6-12 months after completion (roughly late 2027 to early 2028) and then annually if normal, with CBC and LDH every 3 months; I will not do routine interim scans beyond the one planned at cycle 2 and will not do routine imaging every 2-3 months in the first year, per current NCCN guidance that favors a single post-treatment PET over serial surveillance. I will reassess clinically at the tumor board tomorrow (2026-09-18) with exam and repeat labs, since LDH rose from 680 to 735 U/L in 13 days, to confirm there has been no interval progression requiring urgent treatment.
pretreatment_workup: COMPLETED: full-dose PET-CT skull base to mid-thigh (2026-09-05) with the above findings; excisional left cervical lymph node biopsy with IHC, flow and FISH (2026-09-11, amended 2026-09-16); bone marrow aspirate and biopsy right posterior iliac crest (2026-09-12, negative); CBC with differential, CMP with LDH, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, albumin, beta-2 microglobulin (2026-09-03 and 2026-09-16); hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B core antibody and surface antibody, hepatitis C antibody, and HIV 1+2 antibody/p24 antigen (all 2026-09-03 - HBsAg nonreactive, anti-HBc reactive, anti-HBs reactive, anti-HCV nonreactive, HIV nonreactive); transthoracic echocardiogram (2026-09-08) with LVEF 58%, GLS -20%, normal RV and valves, no effusion; ECOG 1, BSA 1.98 m2, weight 79 kg; no known drug allergies; no prior chemotherapy, radiation or malignancy; no diabetes, and no cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease; no diabetes/ocular disease to contraindicate polatuzumab; documented baseline neurologic examination. STILL TO BE COMPLETED BEFORE CYCLE 1: (1) contrast-enhanced brain MRI (no CNS imaging to date; PET is insensitive for intracranial disease and CNS-IPI is 3); (2) baseline 12-lead ECG with electrolytes; (3) baseline quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM), CD4 count and CMV serology before anti-CD20 therapy; (4) current CBC and CMP within 7 days of cycle 1 (last CBC 2026-09-03) and a TSH (last 2.1 in June 2026) - I will continue levothyroxine; (5) hepatitis B DNA quantitation and continued HBsAg/anti-HBc/anti-HBs monitoring (resolved HBV infection, no antiviral prophylaxis required, but anti-CD20 therapy warrants monitoring); (6) dental evaluation, dietitian/nutritional assessment, and vaccination update (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, recombinant zoster - before or early in therapy, no live vaccines); (7) baseline DEXA given 6 cycles of prednisone; (8) urine protein assessment and serum free light chains; (9) an echocardiogram-based surveillance schedule (repeat echo with GLS after cycles 2 and 4 and at completion). Not indicated and deliberately not ordered: bilateral testicular ultrasound (no testicular involvement), head MRI-elsewhere, bone marrow re-biopsy, PET-CT of the brain, cytogenetics/karyotype, PD-L1 testing (no role in DLBCL), and hepatitis C PCR (antibody negative).
supportive_care: Growth factor support is mandatory: pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 2 of every cycle (age >60, bulky disease, and the polatuzumab/R-CHP backbone all confer high neutropenia risk). Tumor lysis prophylaxis given bulky disease with rising LDH and uric acid at the upper limit of normal: allopurinol 300 mg daily starting 2 days before cycle 1 and continuing through cycle 1, oral/IV hydration aiming for urine output >2 mL/kg/h, and twice-weekly monitoring of uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium and creatinine during cycles 1-2; I will add rasburicase if the confirmed ULN shows LDH >2x ULN or if uric acid rises above 8 mg/dL or fails to fall. Infection prophylaxis: trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis (prednisone 100 mg/day for 5 days per cycle x6 cycles exceeds the 20 mg/day for >=4 weeks threshold) held around myelosuppressive periods; acyclovir 400 mg twice daily while receiving intrathecal methotrexate and during any steroid pulse, given plus consideration of fluconazole if neutropenia and high-dose steroids overlap. Antiemetics: ondansetron and a neurokinin-1 antagonist with each cycle plus the scheduled dexamethasone, with glucose monitoring (glucose 104 at baseline) given steroids; continue omeprazole for gastric protection and GERD, continue levothyroxine, and note no clinically significant rituximab–drug interactions. Rituximab and polatuzumab infusion management: acetaminophen, diphenhydramine and corticosteroid premedication, slow rituximab infusion, and a 90-minute infusion time for polatuzumab; teach the patient to report rash, wheeze or fever during infusions. Monitoring: CBC at nadir twice weekly during cycles 1-2 and weekly thereafter with filgrastim rescue if ANC <1,000/uL; CMP and LDH before each cycle; peripheral neuropathy assessment before each polatuzumab dose (he has no baseline neuropathy - new paresthesias would prompt holding or discontinuing polatuzumab); blood pressure and infection assessment each visit, with any temperature >=38.0 C during neutropenia treated as presumed infection with cultures and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics. Because of splenic involvement I will treat him as functionally asplenic: pneumococcal (and meningococcal and Hib) vaccination, explicit instruction that fever >=38.0 C is an emergency with same-day antibiotic dosing, and counseling to avoid animal exposure and to seek care for bites. Ongoing vitals and weight at every visit (weight loss is a response marker here). Vaccination before/early in therapy (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, recombinant zoster) and no live vaccines. Nutrition: high-calorie/high-protein diet with dietitian referral for the 7 kg loss and reduced oral intake; no neutropenic diet restriction needed beyond food safety. Symptom support: scheduled acetaminophen for B symptoms, with the caveat that recurrent fever during neutropenia must be worked up as infection rather than assumed tumor fever. Anticoagulation: if a PICC is placed for 6 cycles of chemotherapy plus intrathecal therapy, I will assess VTE risk (Khorana) and use thromboprophylaxis if indicated, and will plan a line-management and fever policy. Transfusion support only if Hb falls below 8 g/dL (none needed now; no transfusions required). Fertility: at 62 with two adult children, sperm banking is not being pursued, but I will offer and document the discussion. Psychosocial: referral to psychosocial oncology and a hair-loss/appearance clinic before cycle 1, and a plan to keep him working part-time from home.
fitness_and_goals: He is fit enough for full-dose curative therapy. Age 62, ECOG 1 at initial consultation and effectively ECOG 1-2 now (working reduced hours from home, independent in all activities of daily living, no longer hiking, no falls), weight 79 kg (down from 86 kg), BSA 1.98 m2, BMI ~25. Comorbidities are limited and non-contributory: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine (TSH 2.1), GERD on omeprazole (EGD 2019 mild esophagitis, no Barrett's), hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin, and remote appendectomy. No diabetes, no tobacco use, no alcohol excess, no known cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease; creatinine 0.9 with eGFR 96; normal LFTs; HBsAg/anti-HCV/HIV negative; LVEF 58% with GLS -20%. Therefore I do not see an indication for dose reduction, for a less intensive regimen, or for a geriatric- oncology pathway; I will instead add primary-prophylaxis G-CSF, serial echocardiography, and steroid-related glucose/bone monitoring, and I will complete a confirmatory geriatric/frailty screen at the tumor board given age >60 so that a change in function between 09-17 and cycle 1 would be caught. His stated goals are cure, continuing to work part-time from home, remaining mobile for monthly job-site travel, and being well for his daughter's wedding in May 2027. The regimen I have chosen is compatible with all of these: six cycles of 21-day pola-R-CHP started in late September 2026 will complete around March 2027, with alopecia expected around 2-3 weeks after cycle 1 and recovery over 3-6 months, which still leaves him well before the May 2027 wedding and roughly a 6-9 month disease-free interval at that event; I will refer him to a wig/appearance clinic now, and I will reinforce that the intent is cure with a realistic discussion of the ~25% risk of primary refractory disease and the ~30-35% risk of relapse, along with the salvage/transplant and CAR-T options that would remain available if he is not in remission. He asked directly about hair loss and travel, and I have answered both; travel is safe with attention to infection precautions and neutropenia timing, and he should have a written fever and neutropenia action plan before each nadir.
missing_information: No contrast-enhanced brain MRI - no CNS imaging exists, PET is explicitly insensitive for intracranial disease, and CNS-IPI is 3; this is required before cycle 1.
No baseline 12-lead ECG on file (needed for anthracycline/polatuzumab baseline and for monitoring QTc/electrolytes).

Laboratory reference ranges and upper limit of normal for LDH (and other chemistries) are not provided, so the LDH ratio for NCCN-IPI and the LDH >ULN criterion for IPI, and the Cairo-Bishop TLS criterion (LDH >2x ULN), cannot be confirmed.
No baseline quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG/IgA/IgM), CD4 count/lymphocyte subsets, or CMV serology before anti-CD20 therapy.

No quantitative HBV DNA and no repeat HBsAg/anti-HBc/anti-HBs after 2026-09-03 (anti-HBc reactive with anti-HBs reactive suggests resolved infection); monitoring plan for anti-CD20 therapy is not documented.
No CBC since 2026-09-03 and no TSH since June 2026 - a current CBC/CMP within 7 days of cycle 1 and a baseline TSH are needed.

No dental evaluation, no nutritional assessment/dietitian referral, no frailty or comprehensive geriatric assessment, and no documentation of vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, recombinant zoster) prior to immunosuppression.
No baseline DEXA and no defined cardiac surveillance schedule beyond the single transthoracic echocardiogram (LVEF 58%, GLS -20%); no prior echo for comparison.

Tissue was reviewed from the left cervical node only - no biopsy or independent pathology review of the bulky retroperitoneal mass, and splenic involvement is radiologic rather than biopsy-proven; certainty that all sites represent the same DLBCL clone is by inference.
No serum protein electrophoresis, serum free light chains, or urine protein quantification documented.

ECOG performance status has not been re-scored since 2026-09-02 and no interim clinical assessment or repeat labs are documented between 2026-09-17 and the tumor board on 2026-09-18, despite LDH rising from 680 to 735 U/L in 13 days.

No documentation of fertility/sperm-banking counselling (low priority at 62 with two adult children, but should be offered and documented) and no record of a formal discussion of clinical trial screening versus standard chemotherapy.
No baseline hemoglobin/iron studies beyond the marrow report noting increased iron stores consistent with anemia of inflammation, and no plan documented for when to transfuse or to use ESA.
